state.declaration: Right — no more circling, no more asking whoever's nearest. Not the woman restocking wicks, not the board-watcher, not the stallkeeper at the last stall before the bend. The paying one. The notice curling at the corner from the spray, the cellar job, and whoever's name sits on it — that's who I go find, same as I tapped the little hook on the map's margin off the crest. And I put it to them straight, one breath, because I want what 'done' means before I lift a finger: who's actually dangerous down there past the rats, anything with teeth; does 'clear the cellar' count if they bolt into the wall, or the drain, or behind something I can't shift; and what exactly counts as finished — every last one, or just enough that nobody screams when they go down there. Then the money: who pays, when, and what name or token I carry so it's me they pay. Nothing comes off that post until I hear it plain.
